title: Navigation API: Add the ability to navigate to a download or form submission

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#82 — filed by @domenic (2021-03), from an offline suggestion by @annevk.

---

In the spirit of `navigation.navigate()` being "a better `location.assign()`", it could also be able to initiate a download or a form submission:

```js
navigation.navigate(url, { download: true });
navigation.navigate(url, { formData });
```

Both are already achievable by constructing an `<a>` and `click()`ing it, or a `<form>` and `submit()`ing it — so this is an ergonomics/completeness argument rather than a new capability, which also means the security surface should be no worse. The original issue flagged one thing to verify: whether there's a user-activation requirement for downloads that would need to carry over.

**Note on current state:** `NavigateEvent.downloadRequest` exists in HTML today, but that is the *observation* side (telling you a navigation is a download). There is still no way to *initiate* one through `navigation.navigate()`, so this request stands.

Sibling: WICG/navigation-api#101 (extending `<a>` to match `navigate()`'s capabilities), migrated separately — the two are converse halves of aligning the declarative and imperative surfaces.

cc @annevk @domenic
